title: Diwali campaign brief for the agency
scenario: Diwali drives 28% of boAt's annual headphone sales. Last year's campaign was fine but indistinguishable from Noise and OnePlus, ‘premium sound, premium feeling, family moments’. Your CMO wants a brief that gives the agency a sharp creative territory, a do-not-do list, an audience that isn't just ‘young Indians’, and a single-line proposition the agency can't dilute. Brief goes out tomorrow.
badPrompt: write a diwali campaign brief for boat headphones
badOutput:
Brief: boAt Diwali Campaign

Objective: Drive Diwali sales of headphones.
Audience: Young Indians who love music.
Message: Celebrate sound this Diwali.
Channels: Social, video, influencer.
Deliverables: Hero film, social cuts, product shots.

hints.title: Force a do-not-do list
hints.body: ‘List 4 things this campaign must NOT do, e.g., not generic family moments, not premium-sound flex.’ Negatives sharpen creative more than positives.

hints.title: Lock the audience to a person
hints.body: ‘Audience: one specific person with a name, age, and listening context. Not ‘young Indians’.’

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a creative brief for an agency.
Anchor the stake, 28% of annual sales.
Name the differentiation problem, indistinguishable from Noise/OnePlus.
Force a do-not-do list. Sharper than positive direction.
Lock to a single-line proposition the agency can't dilute.
Reference the audience, the agency receiving this brief.
Force a specific persona, not ‘young Indians’.
Specify the brief sections, territory, audience, proposition, do-not-do.
Specify the structure, sections, kept tight.

tipIfLow: Creative briefs from AI default to ‘young Indians, premium sound’. The unlock is naming a specific person (not a demo), forcing a do-not-do list, AND locking a single-line proposition. Sharpness comes from negatives.
goldPrompt: Act as a senior creative strategist. I'm Aarav, brand marketer at boAt. Last Diwali's campaign was indistinguishable from Noise/OnePlus ('premium sound, family moments'). CMO needs a brief by tomorrow. Output: (1) Audience as ONE specific person — name, age, listening context, e.g., 'Rehaan, 22, BCom in Pune, listens on the bus to gym'. NOT 'young Indians'. (2) Single-line proposition the agency cannot dilute (under 12 words). (3) Creative territory in 1 paragraph. (4) DO-NOT-DO list — exactly 4 items (e.g., 'no generic family-around-diya shots'). (5) One success metric.
